## Simple explanation

A node is one of the things represented in a graph. If a graph models a
social network, each person can be a node and each friendship can be an
edge.

## Technical explanation

A graph is commonly defined as $G=(V,E)$, where $V$ is a set of nodes
(also called vertices) and $E$ is a set of edges that connect pairs of
nodes. Graphs may be directed or undirected, weighted or unweighted.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Nodes are the basic units in graph data and graph neural networks. They can
represent users, products, locations, documents, or entities, with edges
encoding relationships that a model can use.

## How it works

Each node may have an identifier and associated features. Algorithms
traverse edges to find neighbors, paths, or connected components. In a
graph neural network, node representations are often updated using
information from neighboring nodes.

## Practical example

In a product recommendation graph, a node may represent a product and an
edge may connect two products that are frequently purchased together. A
recommendation system can use those connections to identify related items.

## Common misconceptions

- A node and its edges are different parts of a graph.
- A node does not have to represent a physical object; it can represent any entity.
- Graph structure does not imply that connected nodes are identical or causally related.
